body.en: *Joints* are points of contact between bones, or between bones and cartilages; the joint acts as a fulcrum for the force generated by muscles. Fibrous joints do not allow any movement; the flat skull bones fuse end-to-end with dense fibrous connective tissue as sutures to form the cranium. In cartilaginous joints the bones are joined by cartilage and allow limited movement, as between adjacent vertebrae. Synovial joints have a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces and allow considerable movement. Examples: ball and socket joint (between the humerus and pectoral girdle), hinge joint (knee), pivot joint (between atlas and axis), gliding joint (between the carpals) and saddle joint (between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb).
body.kn: ಕೀಲುಗಳು ಮೂಳೆಗಳು ಸಂಧಿಸುವ ಸ್ಥಳಗಳು. ನಾರಿನ ಕೀಲುಗಳು ಚಲಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ (ತಲೆಬುರುಡೆಯ ಹೊಲಿಗೆಗಳು); ಮೃದ್ವಸ್ಥಿ ಕೀಲುಗಳು ಸೀಮಿತ ಚಲನೆ (ಕಶೇರುಕಗಳ ನಡುವೆ); ಸೈನೋವಿಯಲ್ ಕೀಲುಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಚಲನೆ. ಚೆಂಡು-ಗುಳಿ: ಭುಜ; ಹಿಂಜ್: ಮೊಣಕಾಲು; ತಿರುಗಣೆ: ಅಟ್ಲಾಸ್-ಆಕ್ಸಿಸ್; ಜಾರುವ: ಮಣಿಕಟ್ಟಿನ ಮೂಳೆಗಳು; ತಡಿ: ಹೆಬ್ಬೆರಳು.

title.en: Disorders of the muscular and skeletal system

body.en: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction, leading to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle. *Muscular* dystrophy is progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle, mostly due to a genetic disorder. Tetany is rapid spasms (wild contractions) of muscle due to low Ca++ in body fluid. Arthritis is inflammation of joints. Osteoporosis is an age-related disorder of decreased bone mass and increased chances of fractures; decreased levels of oestrogen are a common cause. Gout is inflammation of joints due to accumulation of uric acid crystals.
body.kn: ಮಯಸ್ತೀನಿಯಾ ಗ್ರೇವಿಸ್ ನರ-ಸ್ನಾಯು ಸಂಧಿಯ ಸ್ವಪ್ರತಿರಕ್ಷಾ ರೋಗ. ಸ್ನಾಯು ಡಿಸ್ಟ್ರೋಫಿ ಆನುವಂಶಿಕ ಸ್ನಾಯು ಕ್ಷೀಣತೆ. ಕಡಿಮೆ ಕ್ಯಾಲ್ಸಿಯಂನಿಂದ ಟೆಟನಿ. ಸಂಧಿವಾತ ಕೀಲುಗಳ ಉರಿಯೂತ. ಆಸ್ಟಿಯೋಪೊರೋಸಿಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೂಳೆ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ. ಯೂರಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲದ ಹರಳುಗಳಿಂದ ಗೌಟ್.

heading.en: The Skeletal System, Joints and Disorders

tagline.en: The 206 bones of the axial and appendicular skeleton, the skull, vertebral column, ribs, limbs and girdles, the three kinds of joints, and disorders of muscles and the skeleton.

myth.en: The 11th and 12th pairs are false ribs because they do not reach the sternum.

truth.en: Ribs 8–10 are the false (vertebrochondral) ribs: they join the sternum indirectly through the cartilage of the 7th rib. Ribs 11–12 are floating ribs with no ventral connection. In everyday speech 'false' sounds like 'not attached at all'. In NCERT the word means 'attached, but not directly'.

say.en: 206 bones: axial 80 (skull 22, hyoid 1, ossicles 6, vertebrae 26, sternum 1, ribs 24) and appendicular 126.
Vertebrae: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 1 sacral, 1 coccygeal; skull is dicondylic; atlas meets occipital condyles.
Ribs: 1–7 true, 8–10 false (vertebrochondral), 11–12 floating; all bicephalic.
Each limb has 30 bones; femur is the longest; girdles: clavicle + scapula, coxal bone (ilium + ischium + pubis).
Joints: fibrous (sutures), cartilaginous (vertebrae), synovial (ball and socket, hinge, pivot, gliding, saddle).

problem.en: Name the joint used in each action: (a) turning your head to say "no", (b) kicking a football by bending and straightening the knee, (c) bowling a cricket ball with a full arm swing, (d) touching your thumb to each fingertip.

steps.en: (a) The atlas turns on the axis — pivot joint.
(b) The knee moves in one plane like a door — hinge joint.
(c) The head of the humerus rotates in the glenoid cavity — ball and socket joint.
(d) The carpal–metacarpal joint of the thumb — saddle joint.

answer.en: (a) pivot, (b) hinge, (c) ball and socket, (d) saddle

say.en: Let us work this out together. Name the joint used in each action: a turning your head to say "no", b kicking a football by bending and straightening the knee, c bowling a cricket ball with a full arm swing, d touching your thumb to each fingertip.
a The atlas turns on the axis, pivot joint.
b The knee moves in one plane like a door, hinge joint.
c The head of the humerus rotates in the glenoid cavity, ball and socket joint.
d The carpal-metacarpal joint of the thumb, saddle joint.
So the answer is a pivot, b hinge, c ball and socket, d saddle.
